text: Zwracam sie do Autora kanału o pomoc:  Mój komputer przeszedł lekką modernizację, dołożyłem mu trochę pamięci - teraz jest 32GB, i doszły mu dyski ssd wpinane w płytę. Mam mały problem z kartą graficzną , która utrzymuje dość wysokie taktowanie zegarów, mimo braku obciążenia. Karta graficzna to gtx 1080 11GB Titan turbo bost. Rozdzielczość mam ustawioną 1920px1080, i odświeżanie na poziomie 100 Hz. Karta utrzymuje taktowanie zegarów na poziomie : GPU ma 1480 MHz , a taktowanie pamięci na poziomie 5508 MHz, temperatura na poziomie 57 - 58 stopni.Przed modernizacją i wgraniem systemu win 10 pro karta sama z siebie zbijała taktowanie do 400 MHz pamięci i gpu , temperatura spadała do 25 stopni. Zaniosłem sprzęt do dobrego serwisu komputerowego, przetestowali go, i u nich wszystko chodziło elegancko karta zrzucała zegary i nic złego się nie działo. Dodatkowo karta przeszła przegląd, wszystko było w niej ok, pasta , i termopady zostały wymienione. Po podłączeniu u mnie na telewizorze karta przez jakieś 20 minut reagowała na obciążenia, zrzucała zegary, podbijała je , ale po pewnym czasie znów zaczęła utrzymywać stałe wartości zegarów, takie jak opisałem na początku. text:
At launch it had a lot of issues to the point where it wasn't really playable.  That's not really the case anymore, but because of the branching quests and just sheer complexity of the systems, there are still some issues.

It's actually a pretty fun/engaging game if you can get into it, mainly because it does a few things differently.  For instance, your character can't read at the start of the game but over time you will learn new words and eventually stuff that was gibberish is readable.  Also, the alchemy (potions) system is its own little mini-game - instead of simply collecting the mats, you actually have to mix/cook/stir the potion in the right order following the recipe instructions.

The combat system can take a little getting used to but once you master it, you feel like a badass.

Why bother test these cards in 4K? What's the point? There was a time when console players kept saying "30fps is enough and that's all human eyes can detect". Thankfully, that farcical notion is long gone. Now that 144hz monitors (and beyond) are becoming the norm, why use a resolution that cannot even give you 60fps in most games? Neither of these cards are 4K cards! 1080Ti was released over 4 years ago and 3060 is the weakest current generation card. Perhaps top-tier next-gen cards will be able to handle 4K well enough in the future. I don't mean to brag, but on my 3080 I play at 1440p because, frankly, even this card cannot maintain a steady 60fps in most games at 4K.
People need to understand that their gaming experience at the moment would benefit from 1440p resolution, where their fps would remain at or above 60 in a lot of games with available graphics cards.
Let's face it! PC gamers on the whole do not play on 4K TVs. They play on monitors. This means that if their money is burning a hole in their pockets and they cannot get their hands on better graphics cards, they should instead invest on a higher refresh rate 1440p monitor (144Hz or above) and enjoy higher frame rates.

text:
@MatisseXV  There are different perspectives. More importantly different opinions. It's important to realize this and respect others and their opinions.

As you mentioned you just repeated opinions from others, i can respect those from which you just copied their ideas. 

Arguing value when all gpu prices are out of control is in itself crazy. There is no "value" for the cards from the perspective of someone that just wants to game. And your own comments suggest you're a gamer. 

12gb goes a long way for creators, and there may likely be a hack to mine etherium sooner rather than later, but that's just speculation and you can mine almost every other coin on a 3060. 

Like it or not, 12GB >11GB
DLSS 2.0 RTX are valuable to nvidia fans.
And there are plenty of videos depicting 3060 pulling more fps with the latest drivers at 1080p - 4k than a 1080ti (the former FLAGSHIP). Analyzing cost per frame when one card can be had on ebay for 700-800(3060) and the other 800-1000(1080ti) is a moot point.

And what resolution should a 60 series card target? Traditionally it's full hd. The nvidia marketing material is pitching this using steam hardware survey, replacing the 1060. Naturally 1080p is the target and at high fps most likely. CP2077 ultra with dlss is over 60fps in this scenario. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8GQiVyS0zeM
To some people that is their perspective and it's worth it.

I can safely assume from your perspective it is not. That's fine. Not everyone is going to share my opinion or yours. But i will note that we can both agree that 1080ti is still a beast of a card.

So i end by circling back to the beginning of my civil reply to you that there are many people with differing opinions and perspectives on gaming, target fps, resolution, game type, etc.
